candidates.source_name: Global Payments Europe, s.r.o. — Sbírka listin (Collection of Deeds), Veřejný rejstřík

(IČO 27088936, V olšinách 626/80, Praha 10, incorporated 2003-09-24, ex-MUZO a.s.) is the Prague card-processing centre serving issuers and acquirers across CEE. Czech law obliges it to file full statutory annual reports (účetní závěrka + výroční zpráva) into the Sbírka listin. This is the single most authoritative disclosure channel for its revenue, headcount, related-party flows to Global Payments Inc. and auditor commentary — none of which appears in the US parent's segment reporting.

Poll annually around June–December (Czech filing season) and diff the document list.

candidates.source_name: ARES — Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (REST API)
candidates.why_relevant: The entity-resolution backbone for this whole cell. A clean, unauthenticated JSON REST API from the Ministry of Finance: GET by IČO returns legal name, registered address, incorporation date, NACE codes and active-registration flags; POST /vyhledat searches by trade name. This is how you enumerate 'who actually is an acquirer/processor registered in Czechia' rather than guessing from marketing sites, and how you detect new entrants, renames and liquidations. It resolved every actor in this cell (Global Payments Europe 27088936, Global Payments s.r.o. 04235452, Worldline CZ 03633144, Nexi CZ 27391761, Comgate 27924505, MONET+ 26217783, Ingenico CZ 28869591, Euronet Services 25608452, Adyen N.V. CZ representative 19640706).
candidates.access_status: public, free, unauthenticated JSON API; responded HTTP 200 to direct GET and POST during this run
candidates.legal_status: official state open register; open data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Nightly/weekly job: POST {"obchodniJmeno":"<name>","pocet":N} to /ekonomicke-subjekty/vyhledat for a watchlist of brand strings; GET /ekonomicke-subjekty/<ICO> for each tracked IČO and diff datumAktualizace, sidlo, czNace2008 and seznamRegistrací. candidates.source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) — bankovnikarty.cz
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech bank-card industry association: the single best pointer source for this cell. It aggregates the actor map (banks, acquirers, processors, scheme representatives), publishes quarterly market statistics on card counts, terminal counts, e-commerce and cashback volumes, and hosts the industry's press-release archive. It also anchors the events ecosystem (Acquiring Day, Card Forum) where acquiring contracts and processor switches are discussed publicly. The site is current — it links a Visa press release dated August 2026.

A domestically-owned supplier of card/smartcard and payment technology to Czech and regional banks — the kind of vendor whose customer wins are a leading indicator of bank card-platform decisions but which issues almost no press. Statutory accounts plus the register's history are the reliable trace of its scale and ownership.
candidates.access_status: public, free
candidates.legal_status: official public register; public by law
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual deeds poll; pair with the company's own site and with public-procurement records where it supplies state-adjacent institutions.
candidates.discovered_via_method: ARES name search as part of first-principles vendor mapping for the cell
queries_used: ARES POST vyhledat obchodniJmeno=Monet+

candidates.source_name: Ingenico CZ s.r.o. — terminal vendor Czech entity (Sbírka listin)
candidates.why_relevant: IČO 28869591, Lazarská 11/6, Praha 2, incorporated 2009-04-06. The Czech arm of the dominant POS terminal vendor. Terminal-estate refresh cycles and Android-POS migrations are decided jointly with acquirers, so this entity's revenue trajectory is a proxy for Czech acquiring capex. A dated Ingenico press release also sits in the SBK archive, showing this actor does communicate locally.
candidates.access_status: public, free
candidates.legal_status: official public register; public by law
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual deeds poll; cross-reference with SBK archive press releases and Worldline group communications (Ingenico's payment-terminal business history is entangled with Worldline).
candidates.discovered_via_method: ARES name search; press-release trace found in the SBK archive index
queries_used: ARES POST vyhledat obchodniJmeno=Ingenico
href extraction of aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz/akt.htm

candidates.source_name: Nexi Group — press releases and financial press releases
candidates.why_relevant: The only functioning newsroom for the Nexi/Nets group, whose Czech legal entity (Nexi Czech Republic, s.r.o., IČO 27391761) publishes nothing locally. Group-level announcements are therefore the sole narrative channel for what Nexi intends in this market, including any CEE acquiring or issuer-processing contract. The separate financial press-release feed under Investor Relations carries the regulated-disclosure versions.
candidates.access_status: public; both press-release paths responded HTTP 200. Guessed shorter paths (/en/media/, /en/media-and-news/) 404 — the live prefix is /en/media-relations/.
candidates.legal_status: corporate publication; regulated issuer (Euronext Milan) for the IR feed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll both feeds and keyword-filter on 'Czech', 'CEE', 'Central Europe', 'Prague'. Expect low hit density — the value is in not missing the one announcement that matters.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Navigation-link extraction from nexigroup.com after guessed media paths 404'd; confirmed by probe
queries_used: direct fetch and href extraction of nexigroup.com

candidates.source_name: Euronet — Czech operations news (euronetatms.cz) and Euronet Services spol. s r.o.
candidates.why_relevant: Euronet Services, spol. s r.o. (IČO 25608452, Pobřežní 3, Praha 8, incorporated 1997-09-16) is a long-established independent ATM and payments operator in Czechia, and Euronet has been actively buying bank merchant-acquiring portfolios in Europe. Its Czech site republishes group announcements in a Czech context — one observed item covers Euronet acquiring a bank's merchant-acquiring business — making it a live indicator of the 'bank exits acquiring' pattern this cell tracks.
candidates.access_status: public; responded HTTP 200
candidates.legal_status: corporate publication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the news/aktuality section; pair with Euronet Worldwide's US investor releases and with the Czech entity's Sbírka listin (subjektId 492714).
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language search on acquiring contracts with banks surfaced the Czech-site republication; IČO confirmed via ARES
queries_used: akvizice karetních transakcí acquiring poskytovatel Česká republika smlouva s bankou (cs)
ARES POST vyhledat obchodniJmeno=Euronet

candidates.source_name: Registr smluv — Czech public contracts register (smlouvy.gov.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: Czech law requires state bodies, municipalities and state-owned enterprises to publish contracts above a threshold in full text. Card-acceptance and processing contracts signed by public-sector merchants (transport operators, hospitals, Česká pošta, ministries) therefore become public documents naming the acquirer, the pricing and the term — a rare open window on real acquiring economics that no vendor would disclose voluntarily. A Komerční banka contract record was observed in search results, confirming banks' contracts do land here.
candidates.access_status: UNVERIFIED from this environment — repeated direct requests to https://smlouvy.gov.cz/ timed out after 30s with zero bytes (curl exit 28), while a deep contract permalink appeared as a live indexed result. Hypothesis: network/geo or bot filtering on this sandbox, not a dead site. Do not record as dead without a second independent check.
candidates.legal_status: official state register mandated by the contracts-register act; open data with a documented bulk/API interface
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the register's bulk open-data dumps over the web UI; full-text search for 'akceptace platebních karet', 'platební terminál', 'zpracování karetních transakcí' and for each tracked acquirer's IČO as counterparty. Retry connectivity from a different network before concluding anything about availability.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language search on acquiring contracts with banks returned a smlouvy.gov.cz contract permalink; first-principles reasoning about mandatory contract publication
queries_used: akvizice karetních transakcí acquiring poskytovatel Česká republika smlouva s bankou (cs)
candidates.observed_blocker: curl (28) Operation timed out after 30006 ms with 0 bytes received, on two attempts with different user agents; treated as unverified rather than dead

candidates.source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj (public procurement portal)
candidates.why_relevant: Tenders for card-acceptance, terminal supply and payment-processing services run by Czech public contracting authorities are published here with specifications, bidder lists and award decisions. Award notices name the winning acquirer/processor and the contract value — the clearest hard evidence of competitive position available in this market, and an early signal when a public-sector merchant re-tenders and switches provider.
candidates.access_status: public; the tender listing responded HTTP 200. (The separate Věstník veřejných zakázek host did not resolve from this environment — unverified, retry needed.)
candidates.legal_status: official state procurement portal; public by law
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-monitor the tender feed for 'platební terminál', 'akceptace platebních karet', 'platební brána', 'zpracování platebních transakcí'; capture award notices and link the winner back to its IČO in ARES.
candidates.discovered_via_method: First-principles reasoning about who must tender card-acceptance services publicly; confirmed by probe
queries_used: direct probe of nen.nipez.cz

candidates.source_name: Měšec.cz — Czech consumer-finance and payments trade coverage
candidates.why_relevant: One of the few Czech outlets that reports on acquiring market structure rather than only consumer products — observed coverage includes the SIX Payments/Worldline consolidation and comparative testing of card-acceptance fees across Czech providers. It also runs a company-register lookup and a tiskové zprávy section that republishes payment-sector releases, giving both editorial analysis and primary-release capture in one domain.
candidates.access_status: public; the homepage and /tiskove-zpravy/ both responded HTTP 200
candidates.legal_status: editorial publication, copyrighted; summarise and link rather than mirror full text
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/feed or index polling on /tiskove-zpravy/ and on payments tags; keyword-filter for acquirer and processor names. Use for lead generation into primary sources, not as an evidentiary source on its own.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Recurring high-relevance hits across multiple Czech-language searches; confirmed by probe
queries_used: Worldline Česká republika akceptace platebních karet tisková zpráva (cs)
ČSOB Česká spořitelna akceptace platebních karet platební terminály tiskové centrum (cs)

candidates.source_name: Lupa.cz — Czech internet and e-commerce/payments trade press
candidates.why_relevant: Covers the e-commerce payments layer — gateways, PSPs, softPOS and platform switches — which is where Czech acquiring competition is currently most visible. Also carries a tiskové zprávy channel that captures vendor announcements not published elsewhere. Complements Měšec.cz's consumer/fees angle with a technology-and-platform angle relevant to processing decisions.
candidates.access_status: public; homepage and /tiskove-zpravy/ responded HTTP 200
candidates.legal_status: editorial publication, copyrighted; summarise and link
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Feed/index polling with keyword filters on processor, acquirer and gateway brand names; treat as a pointer into primary corporate and register sources.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Probed as a candidate Czech technology/payments outlet based on cell reasoning; confirmed live
queries_used: direct probe of lupa.cz

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch quota (200/200 calls) was already exhausted by other agents before this cell's first query, so no native web search was available at any point during this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Substituted Seznam.cz HTML search (https://search.seznam.cz/?q=...) fetched via WebFetch as the search engine, supplemented by direct HTTP probing and the ARES REST API. DuckDuckGo (both html. and lite. endpoints) served a CAPTCHA challenge instead of results and was not used; the CAPTCHA was not attempted. Mojeek returned HTTP 403. Seznam.cz worked reliably and is, helpfully, the Czech-market search engine, so local-language recall was good — but result depth was limited to roughly the first page per query, and no result-page pagination was possible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Breadth of discovery for this cell is narrower than it should be. Long-tail actors (smaller PSPs, ISOs, bank-internal processing units) and second/third-page results were systematically not seen. A re-run with search budget available should be assumed to add materially to this slice rather than merely confirm it.

negative_findings.description: The seed query used the Czech phrase 'akvizice karetních transakcí' for card acquiring. In Czech financial usage 'akvizice' means a corporate acquisition (M&A), not card acquiring.
negative_findings.result_summary: That query returned mostly M&A and unrelated legal/broker results, plus a Euronet merchant-acquiring M&A item. The productive Czech terms are the English loanword 'acquiring' used as-is, and native phrasings 'akceptace platebních karet', 'přijímání platebních karet', 'přijímat platby kartou' and 'zpracování karetních transakcí'. Queries rebuilt on those terms returned the relevant acquirers immediately.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated collection built on the seed phrasing will have poor precision and will miss the core actors. The glossary for this cell must treat 'akvizice' as a noisy term and prefer 'akceptace/přijímání platebních karet' plus the bare loanword 'acquiring'.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for a Nexi or Nets Czech-language newsroom, press page or local site.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Czech query 'Nexi Nets Česká republika platební karty zpracování transakcí' returned only homonyms — a Google Play listing for Nexi Business, an unrelated Czech IT firm 'Nexineo CZ', 'Nexnet', and a real-estate agency 'Reality NEXI'. No Czech-language Nexi/Nets corporate presence was found. The company's existence in Czechia was established only via ARES (Nexi Czech Republic, s.r.o., IČO 27391761, V celnici 1031/4, Praha 1, incorporated 2005-10-31) and its Sbírka listin entry.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For Nexi there is effectively no Czech-language disclosure channel: coverage must rest on the statutory filings plus the English group newsroom. Also, 'Nexi' and 'Nets' are both high-noise search tokens in Czech and must always be qualified (with 'platební', 's.r.o.', or the IČO) in any automated query.

negative_findings.description: Looked for a Czech-language press/newsroom page belonging to the legal entities Global Payments Europe, s.r.o. and Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o. themselves.
negative_findings.result_summary: None found. Global Payments' Czech communication runs through the marketing site globalpayments.cz (which serves HTTP 403 to scripted requests) and its blog; there is no 'tiskové centrum' or press-release archive for the Czech entity. Worldline's Czech site (worldline.com/cs-cz/home) is a localised marketing page, with press releases only at group level in English. The historical domain globalpaymentseurope.cz no longer serves the company — a fetch returned a TLS certificate mismatch, the certificate covering the unrelated names 0oo1.cz / www.0oo1.cz.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Czech-entity announcements for the two largest actors in this cell are not separately published. Contract wins and platform migrations affecting Czechia must be caught either at parent-group level in English, in the statutory accounts a year later, or indirectly via the SBK/ČTK wires and trade press. Collection design must not assume a local newsroom exists.

negative_findings.description: Several relevant Czech commercial and aggregator domains refused scripted requests.
negative_findings.result_summary: HTTP 403 observed on www.globalpayments.cz (root, /blog, /podpora/dulezite-dokumenty), www.gpwebpay.cz, www.zivefirmy.cz and the bare host aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz (though the archive path /akt.htm on that host fetched fine). These are hypotheses of bot defence, not evidence of dead sites — all four appear in current search indexes and one served content on a deeper path.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for the Global Payments Czech properties requires a headless browser with a realistic fingerprint; a naive HTTP fetcher will silently report these primary sources as unavailable and the cell will look emptier than it is.

negative_findings.description: Multiple plausible URL patterns for corporate and bank press pages returned errors, indicating site re-architecture rather than absence.
negative_findings.result_summary: worldline.com/en/home/newsroom.html -> 404 (correct path is /en/home/top-navigation/media-relations); worldline.com/en/home/investors.html -> 400 (IR lives on investors.worldline.com); nexigroup.com/en/media/ and /en/media-and-news/ -> 404 (correct prefix /en/media-relations/); investors.globalpayments.com/financial-information/sec-filings -> 404 (correct path /all-sec-filings); csob.cz/portal/o-csob/pro-media and csob.cz/pro-media -> HTTP 500 redirect to an error page; kb.cz/cs/o-bance/tiskove-centrum, rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media and moneta.cz/o-nas/pro-media -> 404; cnb.cz/cs/statistika/platebni-styk/ -> 404 (statistics sit under /cs/statistika/menova_bankovni_stat/harm_stat_data/); protext.cz/zpravy.php and ceskenoviny.cz/tiskove/ -> 404 while the deeper paths work.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per the playbook these are hypotheses, not verdicts. Every one of them was resolved to a live path by re-deriving from site navigation or a fresh search — so any monitoring config must include a re-discovery step on 404 instead of retiring the source. The ČSOB HTTP 500 in particular should be retried before any conclusion.

negative_findings.description: Checked whether the CardMag trade-magazine public PDF archive extends to recent years.
negative_findings.result_summary: The archive index at cardmag.cz/pages/cze/archiv.html enumerates issues in the pattern cm<quarter>_<year>.pdf and the visible listing runs to 2018. Probes for cm2_2025.pdf and cm1_2026.pdf both returned HTTP 404. Whether the magazine ceased, moved behind a member wall, or simply changed its filename scheme was not determined.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CardMag is the deepest narrative source on Czech card processing history, so a truncated archive caps its usefulness for recent-period analysis while leaving it excellent for reconstructing the MUZO/Global Payments Europe lineage and older bank-processor relationships. Worth one targeted follow-up to establish the current publication status.

negative_findings.description: The SBK association site links a members-only data area.
negative_findings.result_summary: http://data.bankovnikarty.cz/secure/private.htm is linked from the SBK home page as a restricted area. It was not accessed and no credentials were sought.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The richest granular Czech card statistics (likely including per-member acquiring data) are behind association membership. Open collection is limited to the published aggregate statistics and quarterly press releases; anything finer would require a legitimate membership or a commercial data agreement, which is a procurement decision rather than a collection one.

negative_findings.description: Two Czech public registers relevant to contract evidence could not be reached from this environment.
negative_findings.result_summary: smlouvy.gov.cz (Registr smluv) timed out twice with zero bytes received (curl exit 28) despite a deep contract permalink appearing as a live indexed search result; vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz failed to connect (HTTP 000). Both are recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The contracts register is one of the highest-value indirect sources for this cell because it exposes actual acquiring contract terms signed by public-sector merchants. Its apparent unavailability is very likely an artefact of this sandbox's network rather than the source, and it must be re-checked from a normal network before any judgement is made about it.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank acquiring arms other than Komerční banka (KB SmartPay) and ČSOB (platbakartou.csob.cz) were not individually mapped to a source. Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit Bank, MONETA Money Bank, Fio banka and Air Bank all touch card acceptance or issuing-side processing in Czechia, and several appeared only incidentally (a UniCredit product-terms PDF, a Fio terminal page) rather than as tracked sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one pass per bank in Czech using the pattern '<bank> akceptace platebních karet' plus '<bank> tiskové centrum / pro média', resolve each bank's acquiring subsidiary or partner in ARES, and record both the press channel and the merchant terms-and-conditions PDF path. Establishing which bank uses which processor is the specific output to aim for.

coverage_gaps.description: Issuer processing and card-platform outsourcing — arguably the cell's most strategically important signal — has no dedicated source. No Czech-language term for 'issuer processing' surfaced in any search; Czech practice appears to use the English phrase or to describe it periphrastically ('zpracování karetních transakcí pro vydavatele', 'zpracovatelské centrum').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat this as a glossary gap first: harvest the actual Czech phrasing from CardMag back issues and from Global Payments Europe / Nexi CZ statutory annual reports (where the scope of business is described in Czech), then rebuild queries from the harvested wording. Contract-level evidence will more likely come from the Registr smluv and NEN than from any newsroom.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's Czech-language coverage is solid for acquiring/merchant-facing terms but thin for processing/technical vocabulary, and there is no Slovak-language coverage even though several of these entities (Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi) run Czech and Slovak operations from shared Prague or Bratislava infrastructure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the glossary with harvested processing terminology (see above) and add a small Slovak query set ('akceptácia platobných kariet', 'spracovanie kartových transakcií') plus the Slovak business register, since CZ/SK announcements are frequently issued jointly and the Slovak side sometimes discloses what the Czech side does not.

coverage_gaps.description: No source was found that reveals acquiring market share or portfolio switches indirectly through third-party observation — for example merchant-side gateway/terminal technology detection across Czech e-shops, scheme (Visa/Mastercard) licensee or principal-member lists for Czechia, or PCI DSS validated-provider listings scoped to Czech entities. The 'reveals-indirectly' category is therefore under-served relative to the direct and pointer categories.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate the Czech PCI resource pcistandard.cz linked from the SBK site, the card schemes' published lists of licensed acquirers/principal members for the Czech market, and technology-detection datasets over the .cz e-commerce long tail as proxies for gateway and acquirer share. Each would give an independent read that does not depend on any actor choosing to disclose.

coverage_gaps.description: Because the WebSearch quota was exhausted before this cell began, all discovery ran through single-page Seznam.cz HTML results, direct URL probing and the ARES API. No pagination beyond the first result page was possible and no second search engine was usable (DuckDuckGo served CAPTCHAs, Mojeek returned 403).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available, prioritising second- and third-page results for the six seed queries and adding the corrected Czech terminology. Expect the long tail — smaller PSPs, ISOs, softPOS entrants, bank-internal processing units — to be where the additions are, since the head of the market is well covered by this slice.

coverage_gaps.description: Sbírka listin entry points were resolved and their subjektId values confirmed for seven entities, but the individual filing documents inside each collection were not enumerated, so the recency and completeness of each company's filings is unknown. Czech entities not infrequently file late or incompletely.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each tracked IČO, enumerate the deeds listing and record the most recent accounting period actually filed, so analysis distinguishes 'no disclosure' from 'disclosure not yet due' and flags chronic late filers.

brief: Czech card acquiring and processing has an unusually good disclosure floor and an unusually poor press floor. The floor is statutory: every actor in this cell is a Czech legal entity obliged to file full annual accounts into the Sbírka listin, and ARES plus or.justice.cz resolve all of them cleanly and machine-readably — Global Payments Europe (IČO 27088936, the ex-MUZO Prague processing centre) and its separate acquiring arm Global Payments s.r.o. (04235452), Worldline Czech Republic (03633144, the entity behind the KB SmartPay joint venture with Komerční banka), Nexi Czech Republic (27391761), Comgate (27924505), MONET+ (26217783), Ingenico CZ (28869591) and Euronet Services (25608452). The press floor is weak because none of the three international processors maintains a Czech-language newsroom: Czech-specific announcements surface either in English at parent level (Global Payments IR, Worldline media relations and investors.worldline.com, Nexi /en/media-relations/), or through the domestic industry apparatus around Sdružení pro bankovní karty — bankovnikarty.cz statistics, the flat-file press archive at aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz/akt.htm, the CardMag trade magazine, and the Acquiring Day and Card Forum events — plus the ČTK wires Protext and České noviny. The sharpest and most under-exploited signals are contractual rather than editorial: KB SmartPay and Comgate publish dated, versioned merchant terms that make pricing changes datable, and the public contracts register together with the NEN procurement portal expose real acquiring contracts and award decisions naming winners and values. Two practical cautions carry into collection: the Czech word 'akvizice' means M&A, not acquiring, so queries must use 'akceptace/přijímání platebních karet' or the bare loanword 'acquiring'; and the Global Payments Czech properties (globalpayments.cz, gpwebpay.cz) serve HTTP 403 to scripted fetches and need a real browser fingerprint rather than being written off as dead.
